rv.q: The seriousness of Sweid's intent percolates long after you've left the theatre.
It stays blithe for perhaps too long but gathers force as it becomes more serious.
And in this amusing, poignant and somewhat-slippery hour he details a half century on the planet trying to avoid trouble.
The show celebrates a tolerance and sweetness that seem to belong to an alien land.
In fact, it’s very easy to warm to Sweid the actor.
It marries provocation with emotional intelligence, presenting its arguments in a fresh light and therefore instigating a new line of thought in its public.
Sweid’s warmth and the passion he has for his children’s future offer an optimistic view, suggesting the fence on which he sits is a pretty good place to be.
Between the River and the Sea is thoughtful and personal whilst placing itself well inside the bigger picture.
Between And The Sea is a piece with genuine moments of poignancy, buoyed by a magnetic central performance and some inventive theatrical choices.

cn.t: Critics find Sweid's solo show a poignant exploration of identity that sidesteps its provocative title's promise, offering magnetic performance and inventive staging while wrestling with personal and political complexities through memoir-like storytelling.
